children: Shares of Greenland Energy (GLND), Greenland Mines (GRML) and Critical Metals (CRML) surged on early Monday after investors reacted to a new U.S. security arrangement involving Greenland and Denmark.

Greenland Energy more than doubled, while Greenland Mines and Critical Metals posted sharp gains. The agreement outlines a larger U.S. role in Greenland's security affairs, prompting speculation that resource projects on the island could attract greater strategic attention from Washington.

The deal is expected to be finalized during the United Nations General Assembly. While details remain limited, leaders in Denmark and Greenland said the framework preserves the territory's sovereignty and interests.

Investors appeared to focus on Greenland's importance as a source of rare earths, precious metals and other materials used in defense and energy applications. Greenland Mines is advancing rare-earth and precious-metals projects, while Critical Metals is developing the Tanbreez deposit. Greenland Energy is pursuing oil and gas exploration opportunities in eastern Greenland.
No new project funding, permits or commercial agreements were disclosed as part of the security arrangement.

title: Rare Earth Stocks Soar After Trump's Greenland Security Announcement
